q: 1. The window which is provided in flat roof, is known
explain: A lantern window is a glass structure installed over an opening in a flat roof to provide natural light and airflow to the space below.

q: 2. The vertical sides of openings for doors and window are called ...........
explain: Jambs are the vertical sides of a wall opening for a window or door, which support the lintel or arch above.

q: 3. The vertical member fixed between steps and handrail is known as
explain: Balusters are the vertical posts that support the handrail of a staircase.

q: 4. The joints provided in wooden floors are of ..........
explain: Tongue and groove joints are standard for wooden flooring to ensure the boards lock together tightly and prevent gaps or unevenness.

q: 5. The number of steps in a flight generally should not be less than
explain: A minimum of 3 steps is recommended to make the change in level obvious and prevent tripping.

q: 6. Minimum width of landing should be
options: one fourth the width of stairs
explain: For safety and ease of turn, a landing must be at least as wide as the stair flight leading to it.

q: 7. In any good staircase, the maximum and minimum pitch respectively should be
explain: The ideal pitch (slope) for a comfortable stair is between 25° and 40°.

q: 8. The lower most horizontal piece of a shutter is known as
explain: The horizontal members of a door or window shutter are called rails; the lowest one is the bottom rail.

q: 9. A vertical member placed at the ends of flights connecting the hand rail is termed as ..........
explain: The newel post is the sturdy vertical post at the start, end, or turn of a staircase handrail.

q: 10. From the point of view of maximum day light, the windows in a room should be located on
explain: In the northern hemisphere, northern light is preferred as it provides steady, diffused daylight throughout the day without harsh solar heat gain.

q: 11. The minimum number of holdfasts recommended on each side of a door frame and a window frame respectively are
explain: Standard practice requires 3 holdfasts for door heights and 2 for window heights on each side to ensure stability.

q: 12. The suitable door for entrance in an air-conditioned building is a
explain: Revolving doors act as an airlock, minimizing the exchange of indoor and outdoor air to maintain HVAC efficiency.

q: 13. The pitch or slope of the stair, for comfortable ascent and descent, should be between ..........
explain: A stair slope between 30° and 45° is considered safe and comfortable. Slopes steeper than 45° are too difficult to climb.

q: 14. Approximately triangular-shaped stones used as steps are called ..........
explain: Monoblock steps are solid, single-piece steps, often cut into triangular or rectangular blocks for masonry stairs.

q: 15. In a panelled door, the rails fixed in between the lock rail and top rail are called as
explain: The frieze rail is the intermediate horizontal member located specifically between the top rail and the lock rail.

q: 16. Generally the thickness of rails and styles adopted in a door frame is
explain: For standard domestic doors, a thickness of 30mm to 40mm (3-4 cm) provides the necessary structural rigidity without being excessively heavy.

q: 17. Queen-post trusses are used when the span is ..........
explain: Queen post trusses are suitable for spans ranging from 8 to 12 meters.

q: 18. A truss is called a composite truss when it ..........
options: has two slopes on each side
is a combination of king and queen post-trusses
is made of two different materials
explain: A composite truss uses two different materials, typically timber for compression members and steel/wrought iron for tension members.

q: 19. The window provided on the sloping roof a building is called as
explain: A dormer window is a vertical window that projects from a sloping roof, creating extra headroom and light in an attic.

q: 20. The projection of tread beyond the riser is 'called as
explain: Nosing is the rounded edge of the tread that extends over the riser to provide more foot space and improve safety.

q: 21. The head room in a staircase should not be less than
explain: The minimum vertical clearance (headroom) measured from the pitch line to the ceiling must be 2.1m to prevent tall users from hitting their heads.

q: 22. When a member is subjected to both compression and tension, the type of lengthening joint to be used is ..........
explain: A tabled joint is a scarf joint where the two pieces are notched to interlock, making it strong in both tension and compression.

q: 23. In a stair, the ratio of the vertical distance covered and the horizontal distance occupied by a flight is called as
explain: Gradient is the ratio of Rise to Going (Rise/Going), defining the steepness of the flight.

q: 24. In doors and windows, style is ..........
options: the vertical member of the frame
the vertical member of the shutter
the member which divides the frame into vertical portions
explain: Styles are the outermost vertical members of a door or window shutter.

q: 25. The type of door commonly used for garages, shops, and godowns ..........
explain: Rolling shutter doors are made of interlocking steel slats that roll up, providing high security and space efficiency for commercial use.

q: 26. The window in which the shutters can rotate either horizontally or vertically ..........
explain: Pivoted windows have shutters that swing on pivots fixed at the center (either top/bottom or sides), allowing rotation for ventilation.

q: 27. The usual way of specifying the screws used in wood work is by ..........
explain: Wood screws are primarily categorized and sold by their length and gauge (diameter), with length being the most common specification.

q: 28. A carpentry tools used for making holes is ..........
explain: A gimlet is a hand tool with a screw-tip and a cross-handle used specifically for boring small holes in wood.

q: 29. A window with a fixed glass provided on the flat roof is known as ..........
explain: A lantern window is a glass-walled structure built over an opening in a flat roof to provide extra light and ventilation.

q: 30. A small wooden block hinged on the post outside the door is known as ..........
explain: A cleat is a small block of wood or metal used to secure a door or provide a stop/grip for a closing mechanism.

q: 31. For a span ranging in between 3.5 m to 4.5 m the most suitable type of roof is
explain: A couple-close roof adds a horizontal tie to prevent the rafters from spreading, making it suitable for mid-range spans.

q: 32. The maximum allowable deflection of a timber beam supporting a roof of span L is ..........
explain: According to standard structural codes, the deflection of a beam should not exceed 1/360 of the span to prevent cracking of finishes.

q: 33. The inclined braces used in a truss to prevent the sagging of the principal rafters are called as
explain: Struts are compression members in a truss that support the principal rafters and prevent them from bending.

q: 34. A roof which slopes in all four directions and having flat top is known as
explain: A deck roof is similar to a hip roof but the top portion is kept flat for use as a terrace.

q: 35. A screw with a square head is known as ..........
explain: Coach screws (or lag bolts) have square or hexagonal heads and are designed to be tightened with a wrench for heavy timber joints.

q: 36. In doors and windows, style is
options: the vertical member of the frame
the vertical member of the shutter
the member which divides the frame into two vertical portions
explain: Styles are the outermost vertical members of a door or window shutter.

q: 37. The normal height of the door in residential buildings
explain: A standard door height for residential buildings is typically 2.0 meters (approx 6'7").

q: 38. The type of door used when good ventilation is required in the room and at the same time privacy is maintained
explain: Louvered doors have slanted slats that allow air through while obstructing direct vision.

q: 39. The number of steps in a flight should not be less than ..........
explain: A flight of stairs should have at least 3 steps to be easily recognized as a change in level, preventing tripping hazards.

q: 40. The extreme vertical support to the hand railing provided at the top and bottom of a flight is known as ..........
explain: The newel post is the heavy vertical post at the start and end of a staircase that anchors the handrail.

q: 41. The additional support given to the nosing in wooden stair is known as ..........
explain: A scotia is a decorative moulding placed under the nosing of a tread to provide additional support and a finished look.

q: 42. The vertical intermediate support to the hand railing is known as ..........
explain: Balusters are the smaller vertical members that support the handrail and are spaced along the treads.

q: 43. In a stair the most suitable position to provide winders is ..........
explain: Winders are tapered steps used to change the direction of a stair without a landing. They are safest and most commonly placed at the start (bottom) of a flight.

q: 44. The best spacing of timber piles from center to center is ..........
explain: A spacing of 900 mm (or 3 times the diameter) is generally recommended for timber piles to ensure proper group action and soil stability.

q: 45. The exposed vertical surface left on the sides of an opening after the door or window frame has been fitted in position, is called ..........
explain: The reveal is the part of the side of a window or door opening that is visible between the frame and the outer surface of the wall.

q: 46. The projecting part of the tread beyond the face of riser is called ..........
explain: Nosing is the edge of the tread that extends over the riser to provide more foot space.

q: 47. The vertical members which support the door frame are called ..........
explain: The vertical sides of a frame are referred to as posts (or jambs in some contexts), while styles are the vertical members of the door leaf itself.

q: 48. The external jamb of a door or window opening at right angles to the wall face, is called ..........
explain: Reveals are the vertical sides of an opening that are exposed between the frame and the wall face.

q: 49. The projections which help in securing the head of a door frame to the masonry, are called ..........
explain: Horns are the horizontal projections of the head and sill beyond the vertical posts to fix the frame into the wall.
